plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, MSFU, PLTU) to zero for capital preservation.
Trim QQQI to 20% to reduce concentration and align with the 20% single-name cap.
This plan prioritizes capital preservation and reduces overall portfolio risk.
It aims for a steady, low-drawdown approach by favoring income and broad index exposure.
conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a modest ~1.5%/month return, focusing on capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration. Expect lower volatility and smaller drawdowns.

plan: Trim all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, SPAL, MUU, METU, MSFU, PLTU) to small allocations, keeping combined leverage <=5%.
Trim QQQI to 25% to reduce concentration and align with the 25% single-name cap.
This plan balances risk and growth, blending broad index with quality tech.
It maintains a small cash buffer and keeps total adds <= total trims + buffer.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for ~2.5%/month growth, prioritizing risk management. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while maintaining exposure to quality tech. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns.

plan: Trim QQQI to 25% to cure the concentration breach.
Add to METU, MSFU, and PLTU, pressing into positions that are working.
Increase exposure to leveraged ETFs (SOXL, MUU, SPAL) to lean into growth.
This plan uses leverage and concentration for stretch growth, with strict stop discipline.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets ~4%/month growth, but comes with significantly higher risk. Expect larger potential drawdowns and increased volatility due to leveraged ETFs. Daily decay and rebalancing effects are amplified; strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Sell all leveraged ETFs (SOXL, MUU, SPAL) to zero.
Sell high-beta single names (METU, MSFU, PLTU) to near zero.
Add to QQQI, rotating into income-focused ETFs for steady monthly distributions.
This plan prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income over growth, keeping a cash buffer.
income.read: This income plan targets ~1%/month, focusing on steady distributions and capital preservation. It significantly reduces growth-oriented and leveraged exposure. While aiming for reliable income, distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in market selloffs.
